        ### Question
        A patient is hospitalized for pneumonia. Gram-positive cocci in clusters are seen on sputum gram stain. Which of the following clinical scenarios is most commonly associated with this form of pneumonia?

        ### Options
        opa. Elderly patient who has trouble swallowing and poor dentition
opb. HIV positive adult with a CD4 count less than 150 and an impaired diffusion capacity
opc. An otherwise healthy young adult with a week of mild fatigue, chills, and cough
opd. Hospitalized adult with development of pneumonia symptoms 2 weeks following a viral illness
ope. An alcoholic with evidence of empyema and "currant jelly sputum"

### Reasoning Chains per Option:
CHAIN: "Gram-positive cocci in clusters" -> "Staphylococcus aureus" -> "post-viral pneumonia" -> "hospitalized adult" -> "pneumonia symptoms 2 weeks after viral illness" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Gram-positive cocci in clusters" -> "Staphylococcus aureus" -> "aspiration risk" -> "elderly patient with swallowing difficulties" -> "pneumonia" -> 70%
CHAIN: "Gram-positive cocci in clusters" -> "Staphylococcus aureus" -> "immunocompromised host" -> "HIV positive adult with low CD4 count" -> "pneumonia" -> 60%
CHAIN: "Gram-positive cocci in clusters" -> "Staphylococcus aureus" -> "alcoholic" -> "empyema" -> "pneumonia" -> 50%
CHAIN: "Gram-positive cocci in clusters" -> "Staphylococcus aureus" -> "healthy young adult" -> "mild fatigue, chills, cough" -> "pneumonia" -> 40%
